rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (score 901, best so far). The oval (20/20 finishes, 1.82 s, rms 0.005) and s-bend (20/20, 2.08 s) are solved. The slalom is the remaining gap: 16/20 finishes, 4 off-track, mean 809 against about 950 on the other tracks, with 0.9 line-loss events per run and max_error 0.035 m. Its failures are off-track exits, not timeouts, and finishing trials take 2.5 s, so the time budget is tight but not the main limit. The trend from iterations 3 to 5 (sensor lead 0.04 to 0.06 to 0.07 m, with kd raised to 0.8 and then 1.0) supports H6: the robot reacts late to sharp alternations, and more lead plus damping reduces this. The sensor y-range allows up to 0.08 m, so this iteration moves the sensors to y = 0.08 and changes nothing else, to isolate the lead effect. Geometry other than y, the sensor span (+/-0.045 m), weights, kp 2.0, ki 0.05, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.0 and line_loss are unchanged. I did not raise base_speed, because slalom finishes already take about 2.5 s and a faster run risks more line loss. Expected result: slalom off-track count falls from 4 to 0-2 and slalom progress rises toward 0.98, with the oval and s-bend staying near their current scores. Risks: the forward sensors may lose the line on the tightest bend (H7, line loss when the line leaves the span), and the extra lead could add overshoot on the oval. Hypotheses: H6, more lead cuts slalom off-track exits; H7, line-loss events come from the line leaving the sensor span. Measurements wanted next: slalom completion, progress and max_error to test H6; line_loss_events on the slalom and s-bend to test H7; steering_oscillation to check whether the extra lead adds jitter; and completion_time on the slalom to confirm it stays under 3 s.
